analysis.title: Derivatives Market Overview, October 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 0.93% in October to 7,580.07, while the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.65% and ended nearly 10% below its October high. The selloff was led by the technology sector.
On October 30 the NDX fell 3.5%, its worst day since June. One-month NDX implied volatility rose more than four volatility points and closed at the 85th percentile on a one-year lookback.
QQQ options volume rose 12% from September and surged 66% on October 30 versus the prior five-day average.

The NDX-SPX volatility spread widened to nearly 10 volatility points, close to double its early-October level. Implied and realized volatility both rose faster for NDX than SPX, which the report reads as NDX's greater sensitivity to the AI theme.
VIX rose 3.08 points in October to 19.42. S&P 500 30-day realized volatility was 10.79%.
Treasury yields retraced much of their September increase, with the 2-year yield 30 bps lower on the month. The MOVE Index fell 10.25 points to 100.20.

In USD swaption skew, short-dated expiries on short tails repriced so receivers traded at a premium to payers. The 3Mx1Y and 3Mx2Y 25-bp risk reversals turned negative, while the 3Mx5Y stayed near zero. The report reads this as demand tied to the near-term policy path, not a reassessment of long-term rates.

U.S. equity financing term structure inverted at the end of October because the front end priced the higher cost of financing long positions over year-end. The rest of the curve moved lower and traded in line with two-year medians for the first time since May.

Year-end financing spreads are below the levels of the prior two years after running above them for much of the summer. Asset manager net S&P 500 futures positioning fell 8.6% from its May high and U.S. levered equity ETF AUM fell 25% from its June peak. Heavy IPO issuance in the rest of the year could weigh on dealer balance sheets and reduce financing appetite.

China A-share index financing shows a persistent dislocation. A one-year total return swap on the CSI 500 pays SOFR minus 1086 bps, so a long investor collects roughly 6.75%. Onshore market-neutral funds hedge by selling index futures, and limited foreign access and difficult short selling keep the basis from closing.

sector_views.rationale: The report describes technology leading the October equity selloff and NDX volatility rising faster than SPX. It states no rating or view on the sector.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields retraced much of the September increase.
Rate volatility eased over the month.
Equity implied volatility rose as the technology selloff developed.

risk_factors: IPOs slated for the rest of the year could weigh on dealer balance sheets and reduce financing appetite into year-end.
The front end of the equity financing curve is pricing a higher cost of financing long positions over year-end.
NDX is more sensitive to the AI theme than SPX, so volatility there can rise faster.
